belief: I'm useless to the church now.
origins: When we cannot attend, teach, serve, or give as before, we may feel invisible to the church. Sometimes churches fail to include those who are limited.
teaches: “The parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable.” “Now to each one the manifestation of the Spirit is given for the common good.” “Carry one another’s burdens.” Those who are ill can pray, encourage, give wisdom, and remind a congregation that the body includes the weak. The church also has a duty to care for the sick: “I was sick and you looked after Me.” You have a place, and the church should make room.
self_statements: The church does not need me.
I am a burden to the church.
errors: Believing I am either active or useless.
Predicting that the church will forget me.
Feeling sidelined and concluding I am useless.
questions: What roles can I still do, such as prayer, calls, and notes?
Have I told my church how I can participate?
What does Scripture say about weaker members?
What would I tell a friend in my situation?
Who in church could help me stay connected?
truth: The body of Christ needs its weaker members. I can pray, encourage, and share my story. I can tell my church what I need and what I can give.
hw_truths: I have a gift for the common good.
The church should visit the sick.
I am part of the body.
log: Each week, note one contribution to the church.
actions: Share your limits and what you can offer.
Choose a ministry to pray for.
prayer: Lord, I feel useless to Your church. Show me my place, and help the church embrace weaker members like me. Amen.
